item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 101735
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Sat Oct 10 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Rachel, located several hundred miles southwest of Punta
Baja, Mexico, and on Hurricane Simon, located about one hundred
miles south-southwest of Manzanillo, Mexico.

South of Southwestern Mexico:
An area of low pressure is forecast to develop south or southwest of
the coast of Mexico by early next week. Environmental conditions are
expected to be conducive for gradual development thereafter, and a
tropical depression is likely to form by the middle or latter half
of next week as the system moves generally west-northwestward at
around 10 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

$$
Forecaster Papin

item.title: Tropical Storm Rachel Public Advisory Number 55
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Sat Oct 10 2026 
000
WTPZ33 KNHC 102048
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Rachel Advisory Number  55
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
200 PM PDT Sat Oct 10 2026
 
...RACHEL STRENGTHENS SLIGHTLY WHILE QUICKLY MOVING NORTHEASTWARD...
...TROPICAL STORM CONDITIONS EXPECTED IN PORTIONS OF THE BAJA
CALIFORNIA PENINSULA THIS EVENING...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM PDT...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...27.0N 118.3W
ABOUT 255 MI...415 KM SW OF PUNTA BAJA MEXICO
ABOUT 400 MI...645 KM S OF SAN DIEGO CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...65 MPH...100 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNE OR 25 DEGREES AT 30 MPH...48 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...989 MB...29.21 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* West coast of Baja California and Baja California Sur, from Punta
Eugenia northward to the U.S./Mexico Border
* East coast of Baja California, from Isla San Luis northward to
Puerto Penasco
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* Southern California coast from the U.S/Mexico Border northward to
the San Diego/Orange County Line
* East coast of Baja California, from Bahia De Los Angeles
northward to Isla San Luis
* Northwest Mexico from Puerto Libertad to Puerto Penasco
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area, in this case within 12
to 24 hours.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, in this case within 24 hours.
 
For storm information specific to your area in the United
States, including possible inland watches and warnings, please
monitor products issued by your local National Weather Service
forecast office. For storm information specific to your area
outside of the United States, please monitor products issued by
your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM PDT (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Rachel was
located near latitude 27.0 North, longitude 118.3 West. Rachel is
moving toward the north-northeast near 30 mph (48 km/h). A 
northeastward to north-northeastward motion with a further increase 
in forward speed is expected through Sunday. On the forecast track, 
the center of Rachel is expected to approach northern Baja 
California today and move onshore tonight. Rachel's post-tropical 
remnants will then move across the southwestern United States on 
Sunday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 65 mph (100 km/h) with higher
gusts. Some weakening is forecast during the next 48 hours, 
especially after Rachel moves inland over Baja California. Rachel 
is likely to become post-tropical by Sunday morning.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 140 miles (220 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 989 mb (29.21 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Rachel can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP3 and WMO header WTPZ43 KNHC.
 
WIND: Tropical storm conditions are expected to reach portions of 
the Baja California Peninsula within the Tropical Storm Warning area 
this evening and continue into Sunday morning. Tropical storm 
conditions are also possible within the Tropical Storm Watch area in 
extreme Southern California, eastern Baja California, and portions 
of northwest Mexico beginning tonight or early Sunday. Strong gusty 
winds associated with the system are expected to spread over 
interior portions of the Southwest United States, especially in 
areas of higher terrain, tonight through early next week.
 
RAINFALL: Rachel will bring 1 to 3 inches of rain to portions of
Baja California this weekend.
 
Rachel and its associated moisture will also bring rainfall of 1 to
3 inches, with maximum amounts locally up to 5 inches in portions of
the Southwest United States this weekend. This will lead to
increasing coverage of rainfall and potential for significant flash
and urban flooding.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with
Rachel, please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall
Graphic available at
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?rainqpf and the Flash Flood Risk
graphic at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?ero.
 
SURF: Waves generated by Rachel will continue to build along the
coasts of Southern California and northern Baja California today.
These waves, combined with an incoming long-period southerly swell,
will cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Coastal
flooding and erosion are expected to worsen tonight into Sunday
morning as the highest waves coincide with the high tides and water
levels that are already running well above predicted levels.
Moderate to major coastal flooding is expected, with hazardous
coastal conditions continuing into early next week. Please consult
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next intermediate advisory at 500 PM PDT.
Next complete advisory at 800 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Pierce/Cangialosi

item.title: Tropical Storm Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 55
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Sat Oct 10 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 102049
TCDEP3
 
Tropical Storm Rachel Discussion Number  55
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
200 PM PDT Sat Oct 10 2026

Rachel continues to trend toward transitioning to a post-tropical 
storm. Convection remains shallow and has become further sheared 
well northeast of the center due to strong southwesterly shear. A 
1731 UTC ASCAT-B scatterometer pass showed an asymmetric system with 
peak winds of 48 kt located just west of the center. Based on this 
data, the initial intensity was raised to 55 kt.

The initial motion is estimated to be north-northeast, or 025/26 kt. 
A turn toward the north with an increase in forward speed is 
anticipated, as noted in the previous advisory. This change in the 
steering flow is due to the storm's interaction with a mid-level 
cut-off low located to its northwest. The updated NHC track forecast 
was nudged eastward initially, but otherwise closely mirrors the 
previous track and aligns with the latest HCCA aid.
 
Rachel has undergone slight intensification since the previous 
advisory, likely due to its interaction with an upper-level trough. 
The storm is forecast to degrade further given its hostile 
environment, specifically because of strong southwesterly shear. 
Rachel is anticipated to move inland just after 12 h and become 
post-tropical by 24 h. The new intensity forecast is largely 
unchanged.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Rachel is expected to make landfall along the coast of northern 
Baja California at tropical storm strength tonight. Tropical storm 
conditions are expected in portions of Baja California and northern 
Baja California Sur, Mexico, where Tropical Storm Warnings are in 
effect. Tropical storm conditions are also possible in extreme 
Southern California, eastern Baja California, and portions of 
northwestern Mexico where Tropical Storm Watches are in effect.
 
2. Damaging wind gusts associated with Rachel and its remnants are
expected to spread over portions of northwestern Mexico and interior
portions of the Southwest United States, especially in areas of
higher terrain, tonight and Sunday.
 
3. Rachel and its moisture will continue to spread over portions of
the Southwest United States and northern Baja California peninsula.
This will lead to increasing coverage of rainfall and for the
potential for significant flash and urban flooding this weekend.
 
4. Waves generated by Rachel, combined with an incoming long-period
southerly swell, will produce life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions along the coasts of Southern California and northern Baja
California. Major coastal flooding has already been occurring in
some areas, with observed water levels running as much as 1.5 feet
above predictions. Coastal flooding and erosion are expected to
worsen tonight into Sunday morning as the highest waves associated
with Rachel coincide with high tides and already elevated water
levels. Hazardous coastal conditions are expected to continue into
early next week. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  10/2100Z 27.0N 118.3W   55 KT  65 MPH
 12H  11/0600Z 30.4N 116.3W   50 KT  60 MPH
 24H  11/1800Z 36.3N 114.1W   40 KT  45 MPH...POST-TROPICAL
 36H  12/0600Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Pierce/Cangialosi

SUMMARY OF 1200 PM CST...1800 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...17.4N 104.8W
ABOUT 115 MI...185 KM SSW OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
ABOUT 215 MI...345 KM SSE OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...150 MPH...240 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...N OR 350 DEGREES AT 1 MPH...2 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...933 MB...27.55 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
* Punta San Telmo to El Roblito
* Las Islas Marias
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* East of Punta San Telmo to Lazaro Cardenas
 
A Hurricane Warning means that hurricane conditions are expected
somewhere within the warning area. A warning is typically issued 36
hours before the anticipated first occurrence of
tropical-storm-force winds, conditions that make outside
preparations difficult or dangerous. Preparations to protect life
and property should be rushed to completion today.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, in this case starting this
afternoon.
 
Additional watches or warnings could be required for portions of the
coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico later today.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1200 PM CST (1800 UTC), the eye of Hurricane Simon was located by 
Air Force Reserve reconnaissance aircraft near latitude 17.4 North, 
longitude 104.8 West. Simon is drifting toward the north near 1 mph 
(2 km/h). A somewhat faster northward motion is forecast to 
continue through the weekend. On the forecast track, Simon is 
expected to be near or just inland of the west-central coast of 
Mexico on Sunday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 150 mph (240 km/h) with higher 
gusts.  Simon is a category 4 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson 
Hurricane Wind Scale. Some additional strengthening remains possible 
today, and Simon is forecast to approach the coast of west-central 
Mexico as a major hurricane tonight or early Sunday. An Air Force 
Reconnaissance aircraft currently investigating the hurricane.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 15 miles (30 km) from the 
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles 
(205 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure measured by Air Force 
reconnaissance aircraft is 933 mb (27.55 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Simon can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP5 and WMO header WTPZ45 KNHC.
 
WIND: Hurricane conditions are expected in the southern part of the
Hurricane Warning area beginning early Sunday, with tropical storm
conditions expected as soon as this afternoon, with these winds
spreading northward thereafter. Tropical storm conditions are
possible within the Tropical Storm Watch area beginning this
afternoon.
 
RAINFALL: Simon is expected to produce rainfall totals of 10 to 20
inches over portions of southwestern Mexico, with isolated maximum
totals of 30 inches possible across portions of Michoacan, Colima,
and Jalisco through Sunday. This rainfall will produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of
steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Simon,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?rainqpf.
 
STORM SURGE: A dangerous storm surge is expected along the
immediate coast near and to the east of where the center makes
landfall. Near the coast, the surge will be accompanied by large and
destructive waves.
 
SURF:  Swells generated by Simon will affect portions of the coast
of southwestern and west-central Mexico during the next few days.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Papin

item.title: Hurricane Simon Forecast Discussion Number 13
item.description:
Issued at 900 AM CST Sat Oct 10 2026 
488 
WTPZ45 KNHC 101458
TCDEP5
 
Hurricane Simon Discussion Number  13
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
900 AM CST Sat Oct 10 2026
 
Simon has gone through some inner-core structural changes over the 
last 6 to 12 hours. After exhibiting a pinhole eye for much of 
yesterday on geostationary satellite, the more recent imagery this 
morning shows a somewhat larger eye that cleared out briefly at 
around 10 UTC. This structure suggests that Simon may have undergone 
an eyewall replacement cycle (ERC) overnight. A couple of microwave 
images that became available after the last advisory also show this 
somewhat larger eye. Since that time, the eye has become more 
clouded over again. The initial intensity is being held at 130 kt 
this advisory, given little change in the satellite intensity 
estimates since the intermediate advisory. An Air Force Reserve 
reconnaissance mission is scheduled for Simon this afternoon and 
will hopefully provide more in-situ data on the hurricane's 
structure and intensity later today. 
 
The hurricane took a bit of a northwestward jog and slowed to a 
crawl since the previous advisory, but the longer-term estimated 
motion is just west of due north at 350/3 kt. The hurricane is being 
primarily steered by a weak mid-level ridge centered to its east, 
which is providing deep-layer southerly flow. Another deep-layer 
trough lies well to the northwest of Simon (which is picking up 
Rachel) but appears too far away to impart much steering, with a 
narrow mid-level ridge parked just south of the Baja California 
Peninsula providing light northerly flow. The net effect is that 
Simon should continue to move northward, but at a rather slow 
forward speed. In fact, the track guidance this cycle has slowed 
down a little more compared to the previous cycle, and the NHC track 
is a little slower and a bit further west in the short-term due to 
the initial position adjustment. This current track forecast still 
takes the hurricane inland over the Mexican state of Jalisco in 
24-36 h. However, it is worth stressing there is still a notable 
amount of track uncertainty, with the ECMWF, HAFS-A, and Google 
DeepMind Ensemble mean (GDMI) keeping Simon just offshore of the 
Mexican coast for the next 48 h, while the GFS, HAFS-B, HWRF, and 
HMON models show Simon moving inland in the next 24-36 h. The latest 
Google Weather Next model (WN3I) attempts to split the difference 
between these solutions and brushes right up along the Mexico 
coastline. The NHC track still remains a bit of the east side of the 
guidance envelope overall, as there is a pretty well-known bias that 
tropical cyclones in this area tend to track east of the forecast 
track due to interaction with the high topography of coastal Mexico. 

The future intensity forecast of Simon is also largely influenced by 
this track uncertainty. Environmental conditions remain very 
favorable, and Simon's intensity will likely be controlled by 
inner-core related fluctuations today. However, as Simon approaches 
the coast of Mexico, the higher terrain will likely start to impinge 
on its outer circulation, where downslope subsidence may start to 
occur. This terrain effect will likely cause its wind field core to 
shrink in size and ultimately result in some weakening, even before 
the hurricane moves near or onshore of the Mexican coastline. Thus, 
weakening is now shown in 24 h, with more substantial weakening 
occurring after Simon's core is forecast to move onshore. It is 
worth stressing that this intensity forecast contains a lot of 
uncertainty, and if Simon remains offshore, it could remain stronger 
than shown in this forecast. This scenario is highlighted by the   
06 UTC HAFS-A forecast which keeps Simon a significant hurricane 
since it remains just offshore. Ultimately, the intensity forecast 
remains quite similar to the prior one after land interaction 
begins, with Simon expected to dissipate over the higher terrain of 
Mexico after 60 h.
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Catastrophic wind and life-threatening storm surge impacts are 
likely along a portion of the west-central coast of Mexico, and a 
Hurricane Warning is in effect from Punta San Telmo to El Roblito. 
Preparations to protect life and property should be completed today.
 
2. Heavy rainfall associated with Simon will impact portions of
southwestern Mexico through this weekend. This rainfall will produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of
steep terrain.
 
3. Swells will affect portions of the southwestern and west-central
coast of Mexico through the weekend. These swells are likely to
cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please
consult products from your local weather office.
